After that, the dots are: c5 (37), c6 (43). Click the dot c5 (16,40), then click c4 (16,32) → merge into c4.
After that, the top = a single dot at c4 (gray). Then move the lock to the top end and check for completion.
Wait — but at t22, after the final merge, the level didn't complete, and the lock was in the center. This time, after the final merge, move the lock to the top end (15,55): from (33,31): RIGHT×4 → (33,55), UP×3 → (15,55).

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def dots(f):
    out=[]
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['pixels']==12 and n['color'] in ('N','g'):
            b=n['boundary']; out.append((n['color'], min(p[0] for p in b), min(p[1] for p in b)))
    return sorted(out)
def lock(f):
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='O':
            b=n['boundary']; return (min(p[0] for p in b), min(p[1] for p in b))
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':26}])
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':40}])
print('after m2:', dots(current_frame))
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':40}])
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':32}])
print('after m3:', dots(current_frame), 'lc=', last_action_result.get('level_completed'))
# move lock to top end
action(['RIGHT','RIGHT','RIGHT','RIGHT','UP','UP','UP'])
print('lock:', lock(current_frame), 'lc=', last_action_result.get('level_completed'), 'done=', last_action_result.get('done'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
